# Cylinder bounds are mislabeled in Voxel Inspector

### What happened?

For cylinders, the Voxel Inspector's Bounds and Clipping panels should let you independently
adjust the shape's height range and its angular range. The screenshots below show the current
behavior.

![Image](/app/.harbor_assets/bug_screenshot_1.png)

![Image](/app/.harbor_assets/bug_screenshot_2.png)

### Other things noticed while investigating

- Some checkboxes in the Display panel end up in the opposite state from the one selected.
- The Inspector sometimes shows the wrong shape's Bounds/Clipping editor for the loaded primitive.
- Some sliders in the Transform panel rotate the primitive around the wrong axis.
- After switching to a different voxel primitive, the Shader panel can still show status left
  over from the previous one.

FROM node:22-bookworm

# System deps: git for the anti-cheat re-init below, python3/build-essential for any native npm
# deps, and Chromium + the shared libs it needs to run headless (this task's spec drives the
# real VoxelInspectorViewModel class through Cesium's own Karma/Jasmine harness -- it needs a
# real browser runtime, even though (unlike this repo's other karma tasks) it never opens a
# WebGL context: the class under test only ever calls `scene.requestRender()` on its `scene`
# argument, so a lightweight mock scene suffices and no createScene()/canvas is involved).
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git \
    python3 \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    chromium \
    fonts-liberation \
    libasound2 \
    libatk-bridge2.0-0 \
    libatk1.0-0 \
    libcups2 \
    libdbus-1-3 \
    libdrm2 \
    libgbm1 \
    libgtk-3-0 \
    libnspr4 \
    libnss3 \
    libx11-xcb1 \
    libxcomposite1 \
    libxdamage1 \
    libxfixes3 \
    libxrandr2 \
    libxshmfence1 \
    xdg-utils \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# karma-chrome-launcher (used by this repo's `gulp test` / `npm test`) resolves the browser via
# CHROME_BIN first, falling back to google-chrome/google-chrome-stable on PATH -- neither exists
# on Debian, so point it at the Chromium package installed above. --no-sandbox is required to
# run Chrome as root inside a container.
ENV CHROME_BIN=/usr/bin/chromium
ENV CHROMIUM_BIN=/usr/bin/chromium
ENV CHROME_FLAGS="--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage"
# Skip the repo's own `npm install` step re-downloading Playwright's browser fleet (Chrome for
# Testing/Firefox/WebKit/ffmpeg) via its `prepare` lifecycle script -- none of Playwright's
# browsers are used by the Karma/Jasmine spec suite this task verifies against; only Chromium
# (installed above) is needed. The repo's "prepare" script is `gulp prepare && husky &&
# playwright install --with-deps`; CI=true/HUSKY=0 make husky's own install succeed, but that
# alone is NOT sufficient -- see the zip.js override below for the real trigger of `gulp
# prepare` itself failing outright (which, per this repo's own banked history, is what actually
# matters here: an earlier failure in the `&&` chain aborts before playwright install is even
# reached, so PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD is kept only as defense-in-depth).
ENV CI=true
ENV HUSKY=0
ENV PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1

WORKDIR /app

# [IMPORTANT] Copy bug patches to a TEMP path (not into /app) so they can be applied into the
# base snapshot below and never reach the agent-visible tree.
COPY assets/bugs/ /tmp/bugs/

# Clone and pin to the base commit (still with real .git/history here, so `npm pkg set` below
# just edits a tracked file in a normal working tree). base_commit is the exact merge-base of
# PR #12522 (confirmed via `gh api repos/CesiumGS/cesium/compare/<base>...<pr-head-sha>`
# returning ahead_by=7, behind_by=0, merge_base_commit=<base> -- matching the PR's own 7 commits
# exactly).
RUN git clone https://github.com/CesiumGS/cesium /app \
 && git -C /app checkout 88bfd9547927bbdcb2cbdfd1950ba8b0d275ff32

# Pin @zip.js/zip.js to the last release whose dist/ output still ships z-worker-pako.js, BEFORE
# the one-and-only `npm install` below. packages/engine declares "^2.7.34" at this base commit
# and no lockfile is committed upstream, so a plain `npm install` resolves the newest matching
# version -- @zip.js/zip.js 2.8.x (confirmed empirically while authoring this task: 2.8.36, the
# version this repo's other tasks pin for THEIR later base commits, does NOT ship
# dist/z-worker-pako.js at all under this "^2.7.34" range's vintage) breaks gulp's `prepare` copy
# step with ENOENT. 2.7.73 (the newest 2.7.x release) still ships the expected dist layout.
# Pinning correctly BEFORE the install that runs life-cycle scripts avoids the ENOENT outright.
RUN npm pkg set "overrides[@zip.js/zip.js]=2.7.73"

# [IMPORTANT] Apply every additional injected bug patch BEFORE the harbor_base snapshot below,
# so each defect becomes part of harbor_base (the exact state the model starts from). These are
# hand-authored regressions layered on top of the real, historical #12521 regression that is
# already present in the base_commit source itself (the cylinder height/angle mislabeling this
# task's issue report describes) -- unlike that one, these four have no upstream commit to pin
# to, so they ship as patches here instead.
RUN for p in /tmp/bugs/*.patch; do git -C /app apply "$p" || patch -p1 -d /app < "$p"; done

# NOW strip .git so the agent cannot inspect the fix PR / future history (anti-cheat), and
# re-init a single base commit + immutable tag so the verifier can reset test files (git apply
# still works without upstream history). This commit is made AFTER the zip.js override edit and
# the bug-patch apply loop above, so both become part of harbor_base itself, not a stray
# post-tag diff.
RUN rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Bake ALL deps at BUILD time -- build has internet, and the agent (solve) phase is OFFLINE
# (task.toml [agent] network_mode="no-network"), so anything the agent's own work depends on
# must already be here. This repo's own npm workspaces install (engine + widgets); no
# package-lock.json is committed upstream (it is .gitignore'd there), so `npm install` -- not
# `npm ci` -- is the correct, repo-native install command (matches this project's own CI in
# .github/workflows/dev.yml).
RUN npm install --no-audit --no-fund

# karma-junit-reporter (the JUnit reporter tests/test.sh needs -- the repo's own karma.conf.cjs
# only wires up "spec"/"longest") is intentionally NOT installed here: it is a test-only
# dependency, isolated to the verify step in tests/test.sh instead of being baked into the
# agent-visible image build.

# Visual evidence, readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/. tests/ and solution/ are
# intentionally NOT copied into the image -- the harness supplies them at verify time.
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/
# [IMPORTANT] Delete the bug diffs from the agent-visible dir so the model can't read the answer
# (the reverse of a bug patch is the fix).
RUN rm -rf /app/.harbor_assets/bugs

CMD ["bash"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for CesiumGS__cesium-12521-mm. Patches in a new, dedicated spec file
# (packages/widgets/Specs/VoxelInspector/__tests__/VoxelInspectorViewModelSpec.js) that drives
# the real, current VoxelInspectorViewModel class (base/fixed/candidate) with a lightweight mock
# scene + mock voxel primitive, runs f2p+p2p through Cesium's own Karma/Jasmine spec harness
# (headless Chromium), and computes a reward from the JUnit report. NEVER greps source for the
# fix -- it runs the tests.
set -uo pipefail
mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/karma-junit.xml       # MUST match verifier.py / run_karma.mjs
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# --- MM SWE submission capture -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Canonical block: must run immediately after `cd /app` and BEFORE the restore loop below, since
# this is the last moment /app is base + agent work. Captures tracked edits plus untracked
# source-like new files into /logs/verifier/submission.patch so a recorded trial can be
# re-scored against edited tests later without paying for another agent run.
_SUB=/logs/verifier/submission.patch
_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index
_SUBSRC=('*.c' '*.cc' '*.cpp' '*.cxx' '*.h' '*.hh' '*.hpp' '*.hxx' '*.inl' '*.m' '*.mm'
         '*.py' '*.rb' '*.go' '*.rs' '*.java' '*.js' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.cs' '*.kt' '*.swift')
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app read-tree harbor_base 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -u 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
mapfile -t _SUBNEW < <(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard \
  -- "${_SUBSRC[@]}" ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' 2>/dev/null)
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -- "${_SUBNEW[@]}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
fi
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app diff --binary --cached harbor_base \
  > "$_SUB" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"

_SUBSKIP=/logs/verifier/submission-skipped.txt
_SUBCAP=/tmp/.submission_captured
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then printf '%s\n' "${_SUBNEW[@]}" > "$_SUBCAP"; else : > "$_SUBCAP"; fi
_SUBSKIPN=$(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
    ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
    ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
    ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
{ echo "# Untracked files NOT captured into submission.patch, newest first."
  echo "# Anything the agent created sorts above build output, which predates the agent phase."
  echo "# total: ${_SUBSKIPN}  (showing at most 40)"
  git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
      ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
      ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
      ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | head -200 \
    | while IFS= read -r _f; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(stat -c %Y "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" \
                              "$(stat -c %s "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$_f"
      done \
    | sort -rn | head -40 | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n",$1,$2,$3}'
} > "$_SUBSKIP" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$_SUBCAP"

_SUBSZ=$(wc -c < "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "$_SUBSZ" -gt 5242880 ]; then
  { echo "SUBMISSION CAPTURE SUPPRESSED: ${_SUBSZ} bytes exceeds the 5MB cap."
    echo "Directories contributing to the discarded patch:"
    grep -a "^diff --git" "$_SUB" | sed 's#^diff --git a/##; s# b/.*##; s#/[^/]*$##' \
      | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
  } > "$_SUB.suppressed" 2>/dev/null
  : > "$_SUB"
  echo "== submission.patch SUPPRESSED (${_SUBSZ} bytes > 5MB cap) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
else
  echo "== captured submission.patch (${_SUBSZ} bytes, $(grep -ac '^diff --git' "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) files) ==" \
    | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
fi

# Robustness + idempotency: restore EVERY path test.patch touches to its pristine base state BEFORE
# applying, so (a) agent edits to tests can't change scoring and (b) the apply stays idempotent on
# re-runs. Read paths from the `diff --git a/... b/...` headers (present for text, BINARY, renamed,
# and deleted entries) -- NOT `+++ b/`, which is ABSENT for binary and renames.
_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done
git -C /app clean -fdq -- $(printf '%s\n' $_patch_paths | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u) 2>/dev/null || true

# Anti-tamper: the whole run depends on the repo's own spec plumbing (Specs/karma.conf.cjs,
# gulpfile.js, packages/widgets/Specs/**, packages/engine/Specs/**). Restore every tracked file
# under both spec trees to harbor_base so a candidate cannot weaken or delete a guard test, or
# redefine a matcher, on its way to a green run. Tracked files only -- nothing the candidate
# legitimately added under Source/ is touched.
git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- Specs packages/engine/Specs packages/widgets/Specs 2>/dev/null || true
# ...and delete anything UNTRACKED that a candidate dropped into either spec tree. Without this
# a candidate could plant e.g. packages/widgets/Specs/VoxelInspector/__tests__/
# VoxelInspectorViewModelSpec.js full of trivially green `it`s carrying this task's identifiers;
# the isolation step below moves aside every OTHER spec file, but a planted file at the exact
# target path is still cheap to delete outright before test.patch re-creates it. Scoped to the
# spec directories only -- /app/.harbor_assets and the candidate's own source files are never
# touched.
git -C /app clean -fdq -- Specs packages/engine/Specs packages/widgets/Specs 2>/dev/null || true

echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# Test-only dep, installed HERE rather than baked into the image build: a JUnit reporter for
# karma, since the repo's own karma.conf.cjs only wires up "spec"/"longest" reporters. Internal
# to the test harness, unaffected by whatever the candidate's fix touches. The verifier phase has
# network_mode="public" per task.toml (only the agent/solve phase is sealed with "no-network"),
# so it's safe to install at verify time instead of shipping it in the agent-visible image.
echo "== installing test-only dep: karma-junit-reporter ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund --no-save "karma-junit-reporter@2.0.1" \
  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not install karma-junit-reporter" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# --- Isolate the target spec file --------------------------------------------------------------
# Cesium's widgets spec bundle (packages/widgets/Build/Specs/*) is regenerated on every
# `gulp build --workspace @cesium/widgets` from a glob over ALL packages/widgets/Specs/**/*Spec.js
# files. Temporarily relocate every OTHER *Spec.js file so the rebuilt bundle -- and therefore the
# karma run -- covers ONLY packages/widgets/Specs/VoxelInspector/__tests__/
# VoxelInspectorViewModelSpec.js (where every f2p/p2p identifier lives; matched by full PATH, not
# by basename, so a planted same-named file elsewhere in the tree is relocated like any other
# spec), instead of the whole widgets suite. Restored unconditionally on exit; this only changes
# which spec files get bundled/run, never any test's own behavior or source.
STAGE="$(mktemp -d)"
restore_specs() {
  if [ -d "$STAGE" ]; then
    ( cd "$STAGE" && find . -type f -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        rel="${f#./}"
        mkdir -p "/app/packages/widgets/Specs/$(dirname "$rel")"
        mv "$f" "/app/packages/widgets/Specs/$rel"
      done )
    rm -rf "$STAGE"
  fi
  ensure_reward
}
trap restore_specs EXIT

while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  rel="${f#packages/widgets/Specs/}"
  mkdir -p "$STAGE/$(dirname "$rel")"
  mv "$f" "$STAGE/$rel"
done < <(find packages/widgets/Specs -iname "*Spec.js" \
           ! -path "packages/widgets/Specs/VoxelInspector/__tests__/VoxelInspectorViewModelSpec.js" -print0)

echo "== building engine index/exports (widgets imports @cesium/engine) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
npx gulp build --workspace @cesium/engine >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: gulp build (engine) failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "== building widgets spec bundle (isolated to VoxelInspectorViewModelSpec.js) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
npx gulp build --workspace @cesium/widgets >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: gulp build (widgets) failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "== running f2p + p2p tests (karma/jasmine) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Node's ESM resolver walks up from the SCRIPT's own directory looking for node_modules --
# it never consults cwd or NODE_PATH for `import` (unlike CJS `require`). /tests is not
# inside /app, so `node /tests/run_karma.mjs` can't see /app/node_modules/karma. Copy the
# script into /app (where node_modules lives) before running it.
cp /tests/run_karma.mjs /app/.harbor_run_karma.mjs

run_suite() {
  node /app/.harbor_run_karma.mjs >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
    || echo "(tests exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
}

# A runner-level crash (browser failed to launch, karma died before the first spec) produces
# either no JUnit report at all or one with zero <testcase> elements. The verifier cannot tell
# that apart from a genuine all-red base run, so it would silently report 0.0. Retry ONCE, and
# ONLY on an empty/absent report -- never on test failures, which must stay red.
report_has_testcases() {
  [ -s "$REPORT" ] && grep -q "<testcase" "$REPORT"
}

run_suite
if ! report_has_testcases; then
  echo "== JUnit report empty or missing; retrying the suite once ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
  rm -f "$REPORT"
  run_suite
fi
rm -f /app/.harbor_run_karma.mjs

# Put the relocated *Spec.js files back BEFORE the judge computes its `git diff harbor_base`.
# Otherwise the diff spuriously shows every other widgets spec file as deleted (they're sitting
# in $STAGE, not on disk) -- the trap-based restore below only fires on script EXIT, which is
# too late.
restore_specs

echo "== running rubric judge (sub-agent request/rescore; never fatal) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app 2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
fi

echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
python3 /tests/verifier.py --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

115	# to the test harness, unaffected by whatever the candidate's fix touches. The verifier phase has

117	# so it's safe to install at verify time instead of shipping it in the agent-visible image.

119	npm install --no-audit --no-fund --no-save "karma-junit-reporter@2.0.1" \

123	# --- Isolate the target spec file --------------------------------------------------------------

128	# VoxelInspectorViewModelSpec.js (where every f2p/p2p identifier lives; matched by full PATH, not

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Report -> reward for CesiumGS__cesium-12521-mm. Behavioral only: reads the JUnit report the
paired test.sh produced (Karma/Jasmine, real headless-Chromium DOM -- no WebGL needed) and the
f2p/p2p identifiers from config.json. NEVER inspects source -- only test outcomes.

Reward policy is BINARY, not partial credit: tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test
passes AND every p2p test still passes; a strict subset of f2p passing is 0.0, not a fraction.
Partial credit would let a half-fix read as "solved" to pass@k, and nothing is lost by
collapsing it because f2p_passed/f2p_total and p2p_passed/p2p_total carry the detail. reward is
the same value, zeroed only when the rubric judge explicitly failed a criterion -- a "pass" or
"not graded" (-1) verdict never lowers the score, since the judge must never penalise a run it
could not grade. This task ships no rubric layer, so rubric is always "not graded" (-1) and
reward == tests_passed unconditionally.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
F2P = CONF["f2p"]
P2P = CONF["p2p"]
REPORT = "/logs/verifier/karma-junit.xml"  # keep in sync with test.sh / run_karma.mjs
REWARD_TXT = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
REWARD_JSON = "/logs/verifier/reward.json"


def load_junit():
    """Return {test_identifier: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} parsed from the karma-junit report.

    karma-junit-reporter (2.0.1, pinned in this task's Dockerfile) can crash MID-WRITE for a
    SPECIFIC <testcase>'s <failure> element when that failure's own message contains a
    control character illegal in XML 1.0 -- confirmed empirically while authoring this task: a
    genuine GLSL shader-compile RuntimeError, whose driver-provided "Compile log:" text tripped
    node_modules/xmlbuilder's XMLStringifier.assertLegalChar. The crash is caught PER TESTCASE
    (unlike the whole-run captureConsole crash banked for this repo's other tasks -- the run
    continues to the next spec), but it leaves that one <testcase> with NO <failure> child at
    all, even though the enclosing <testsuite failures="N"> attribute still counts it correctly.
    A naive per-testcase-only scan then silently reports that spec as a PASS -- verified directly
    against this task's own ab2 anti-bandaid probe (a deliberately broken/uncompilable shader):
    all 6 testcases showed zero <failure> children while the suite attribute said failures="6".
    Guard: if the suite-level failure+error count exceeds what is actually visible per
    testcase, we cannot tell WHICH testcases lost their marker, so every testcase in that
    (corrupted) report is treated as a failure rather than risk crediting a spec that never
    actually passed.
    """
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    root = tree.getroot()
    declared_bad = 0
    for suite in root.iter("testsuite"):
        for attr in ("failures", "errors"):
            try:
                declared_bad += int(suite.get(attr, 0) or 0)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                pass
    testcases = list(tree.iter("testcase"))
    observed_bad = sum(1 for tc in testcases if any(c.tag in ("failure", "error") for c in tc))
    corrupted = declared_bad > observed_bad
    for tc in testcases:
        name = f"{tc.get('classname', '')} {tc.get('name', '')}".strip()
        if any(c.tag == "skipped" for c in tc):
            results[name] = "skip"
        elif any(c.tag in ("failure", "error") for c in tc):
            results[name] = "fail"
        elif corrupted:
            results[name] = "fail"
        else:
            results[name] = "pass"
    return results


def matched(idents, results):
    """Match each configured identifier against reported test names (substring tolerant)."""
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if ident in k), None)
        out[ident] = hit or "missing"
    return out


def rubric_verdict(raw):
    """"pass"/"fail" (case-insensitive) -> that verdict; anything else -> None ("not graded").

    This task ships no rubric layer (tests/rubrics.json, tests/judge.py), so test.sh always
    passes an empty string here and this always resolves to None. Kept as an explicit gate,
    not dead code, in case a rubric is added back later.
    """
    value = (raw or "").strip().lower()
    return value if value in ("pass", "fail") else None


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy: binary, per the module docstring above."""
    solved = f2p_total > 0 and f2p_passed == f2p_total and p2p_passed == p2p_total
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    reward = 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed
    return reward, tests_passed


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--rubric", default="", help='"pass" | "fail" | "" (not graded)')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rubric = rubric_verdict(args.rubric)

    results = load_junit()
    f2p = matched(F2P, results)
    p2p = matched(P2P, results)
    f2p_passed = sum(1 for v in f2p.values() if v == "pass")
    p2p_passed = sum(1 for v in p2p.values() if v == "pass")

    reward, tests_passed = canon_reward(f2p_passed, len(F2P), p2p_passed, len(P2P), rubric)

    detail = {
        "reward": reward,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f2p_passed,
        "f2p_total": len(F2P),
        "p2p_passed": p2p_passed,
        "p2p_total": len(P2P),
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    }

    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(REWARD_JSON), exist_ok=True)
    with open(REWARD_JSON, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(detail, fh, indent=2)
    with open(REWARD_TXT, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(str(reward))
    print(json.dumps({**detail, "f2p": f2p, "p2p": p2p}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
